output.summary: Approved the G1021 design. The spec's premise is corrected: integrate already handles CONFLICTING/DIRTY; the gap is GitHub's lazy UNKNOWN mergeability and an unseen head, which fell through to 'checks pending'. The fix: a local git merge-tree pre-check when the PR targets the integration branch, giving a conflict finding on base at once; ordered waits for head-not-seen and UNKNOWN, bounded by ci_timeout; a human question when no check appears within min(15, ci_timeout) minutes; merge state in the pending reason; a mergeable_lag fake-gh fault and tests; a REPAIR recipe. The integration tip stays out of base's fingerprint. The reviewer's two implementation notes go to implement. Decision made by Claude (root agent) under the owner's standing delegation for Release 1.

Integrate already handles CONFLICTING/DIRTY; the incident came from GitHub's lazy mergeability: the pr view straight after creating #747/#748 returned UNKNOWN, which fell through to 'required checks pending'. The design adds a deterministic local merge-tree conflict check against the fetched integration tip, explicit short waits for UNKNOWN and an unseen head, a 15-minute 'no checks at all' human escalation, and a REPAIR.md recipe. Decision: base stays non-stale when dev moves (the integration tip is not a base input, by design, to avoid cascading re-runs); conflicts reach base through integrate/merge findings.

Approved. The corrected premise checks out at read_dev: integrate.py 171-175 and test_conflicting_pr_into_dev_is_a_base_finding already handle CONFLICTING/DIRTY, and the G1016/G1000 records show a single UNKNOWN-era 'checks pending' poll. Limiting the local merge-tree pre-check to target == I gives GitHub's exact merge semantics and needs no new Git version (MIN_GIT 2.41). It is cheap, and its disagreements with GitHub cannot loop. The waits are bounded by ctx.wait and ci_timeout. The 15-minute empty-rollup question is well gated. Keeping the integration tip out of base's fingerprint avoids staleness cascades across every in-flight goal. Two non-blocking notes are in the report: keep the head-not-seen wait before the GitHub conflict branch, and use --no-messages when listing files.

spec:
Bug found while dogfooding Release 1. After G1014, G1018, G1001 and G1015 merged into dev, the PRs for G1016 (#747) and G1000 (#748) conflicted with dev (GitHub mergeable CONFLICTING, mergeStateStatus DIRTY). GitHub runs no pull_request workflows on a conflicting PR, so no checks ever appear, and git.integrate kept answering 'required checks pending: dev-required-tests' with a retry. It would have waited forever, and nothing pointed at the real problem. github.merge already handles CONFLICTING/DIRTY by raising a conflict finding on the base input; integrate does not.

Outcome:
- After pushing or updating the PR, git.integrate reads `mergeable` and `mergeStateStatus` from the `pr view` call it already makes.
- On CONFLICTING or DIRTY it finishes not-ok with a `conflict` finding on its `base` input, as github.merge does, so `base` re-runs and rebases onto the current integration tip, or asks for a conflict resolution through its existing retry path.
- On UNKNOWN it waits briefly, as merge does.
- A 'checks pending' wait that has seen no check at all after a bounded time, and whose PR is not mergeable, never just waits again.
- Also check whether `base` should already be stale when the integration branch moves while integrate is waiting. It was not offered in this incident. Explain why, and fix it if the design intends it.

Acceptance:
- Fake-gh tests: a conflicting PR gives a conflict finding and base ready; UNKNOWN then MERGEABLE proceeds; a mergeable PR with pending checks still waits.
- A journey: two goals both touch one file; the first merges; the second's integrate sends it back to base, and it then integrates cleanly after the rebase.
- No extra GitHub calls in the common case: reuse the pr view fields.
- Docs: REPAIR.md mentions the case.
title: integrate must detect a conflicting PR instead of waiting for checks forever
